All notable changes to the GLOW are documented in this file. The format is based
on Keep a Changelog.

Releases are tagged in the
GitHub repository. Dates are in
Pacific Time (UTC-7).

[Unreleased]

Fixed

  • Include complete ChatGPT, VS Code desktop and VS Code web manual
    walkthroughs in docs/ahg-2026/kit/manual-walkthroughs/, as Markdown and
    offline HTML, for both repository and live-kit access. Keep the matching
    rehearsal scenarios and quick checklist synchronized in S:\ahgtest.
    Generate the manuals from current prompts and Copilot commands with
    scripts/build_ahg_manuals.py; include small numbered ChatGPT paste
    messages, exact interview answers, expected responses, version save checks,
    recovery steps and a written fallback without requiring chat attachments.
  • Remove braille production from AHG alternate-format exercise examples
    and browser prompts; clarify that no braille translator or output is
    required. Keep GLOW Braille Studio and personal assistive technology.
  • Restore the real optional liblouis state after braille availability and
    route tests in web/tests/test_braille.py, preventing randomized local
    test runs from mistaking a leaked mock for an installed translator.
  • Align AHG setup, prompts, cards and facilitator guidance on approved
    tools, optional sharing and a complete written-example route. Require
    practice-file save/reopen checks rather than relying on an AI's Ready message.

  • Add named version downloads on /ahg/assistant, preserve VS Code agent
    history, and save exercise notes for interrupted sessions. Grounded
    comparisons must use the actual first answer; missing answers remain
    incomplete. Require draft review before the final 30-day plan save.

  • Keep the AHG sharing slides, step card, facilitator guidance and
    my-30-day-plan skill consistent: check permission first, allow deferred
    sharing, and only project participants' agents with their permission.

  • Rebuild the /changelog/ page from CHANGELOG.md so recent updates are
    published, remove its duplicate H1, and add tests to detect future drift.
  • Add the changed AHG landing and share pages to the axe accessibility audit.
  • Fix .github/workflows/docs-quality.yml so the editor's Markdown settings
    no longer override the accessibility-only lint rules in CI. A failing
    probe verifies that all seven intended rules are active.

  • Make bare web addresses and inline-code URLs clickable in AHG HTML, Word,
    PowerPoint and library EPUB exports, including addresses in slide text and
    tables. Check live hyperlink destinations in the format gate.

  • Fix a JavaScript string literal on /ahg/share?practice=1 and in the offline
    kit share page that disabled practice selection, template filling, agent
    downloads and GitHub sharing. Add keyboard regression tests for both copies,
    including the downloaded SKILL.md content and prefilled GitHub URL.

  • Clarify that AHG uses prepared assistant prompts without a public directory
    listing, remove stale plugin-directory claims from the assistant and kit
    guide, describe the hosted server's twelve tools and document handling, and
    correct Claude-directory and Codex hook status.
  • Expand ACB, APH, WCAG, BOP and CMS terminology before first use across the
    core forms and result pages, and record the plain-language check as passing.

  • Give Accessibility Agents chat its own page at /accessibility-agents/chat/,
    keep the existing API routes, announce new replies without moving focus, and
    redirect /aa to the Accessibility Agents landing page.

  • AHG library DAISY requests and health checks use the same explicit IPv4
    loopback address, avoiding localhost address-resolution mismatches.

  • Complete the AHG content consistency pass: seven-heading ready check, caption
    source text on both assistant paths, evidence limits, voluntary author credit,
    approved fallbacks and deferred sharing, a timed block-7 plan with partner
    review, and observable learning-outcome checks.

  • AHG PowerPoint tables now allocate each row's wrapped-text height instead of
    equal rows that expand over the links below them in PowerPoint. This preserves
    the layout correction identified on the supplied "On Monday" slide. Reading
    decks turn wide tables into labelled records without reducing type size.

  • AHG step card 7 now matches the eight-question browser and VS Code planning
    flows. Both include campus approval, safe pilot inputs, reviewer roles,
    baseline and day-30 measures, and stop/manual-fallback rules. The tutorial,
    three worked examples and facilitator guidance use the same disability
    resource center handoff. Missing-evidence exercises now accept an appropriate
    request for evidence rather than requiring guesses; grounding is not presented
    as a guarantee of correctness.

  • Complete the AHG content consistency pass: seven-heading ready check, caption
    source text on both assistant paths, evidence limits, voluntary author credit,
    approved fallbacks and deferred sharing, a timed block-7 plan with partner
    review, and observable learning-outcome checks.

  • Readable next-step cards in dark mode. The "What's Next?" card on the
    audit report, fix results and conversion complete pages kept its light fill in
    dark mode, leaving its text at 1.21:1 and the focus ring at 1.98:1. It now has
    a dark fill. The fix results page no longer shows two "What's Next?" sections,
    and the "No file selected" error on the audit, fix and convert forms is now
    part of the file field's description. Found by the manual accessibility checks
    recorded in docs/accessibility-testing.md.

  • PDF output is tagged (#145). Every PDF GLOW renders with WeasyPrint --
    Convert to PDF, the shared audit report's PDF download and the Document Chat
    PDF export -- now asks for tagged output and the PDF/UA-1 variant, so the file
    carries a structure tree (headings, lists, tables, reading order),
    /MarkInfo /Marked true, a language, a displayed title and the PDF/UA-1
    identifier in its metadata. Previously all three wrote untagged PDF. The
    Document Chat export now gives Pandoc a page title and language, which PDF/UA
    needs. The options live in one place,
    acb_large_print.pandoc_converter.write_tagged_pdf, and
    web/tests/test_tagged_pdf.py renders a PDF through each path, checks its
    tags and metadata, and fails if any shipped code calls write_pdf() directly.
    web/requirements.txt now pins WeasyPrint 68 or later, matching
    web/pyproject.toml. A check with PAC or veraPDF is still to be recorded.
  • The user guide is one edition (#147). docs/user-guide.md and the page
    the web app serves at /guide/ held the current guide and then an earlier
    edition, so the heading list showed most sections twice under two numbering
    schemes. The earlier edition is gone. What it had that the current one did not
    now lives in the current edition: heading detection in the desktop app and how
    detection was tested, the APH profile's 1.25 line spacing, how long a
    Whisperer session lasts, the ePub alt text fix, a "Reading the report" heading
    for the finding list, the admin sign-in and dashboard details, and the Product
    Requirements link. The "Keeping your settings across devices" (passport)
    section, which existed only in the served HTML, is now in the Markdown under
    Settings. Sections are numbered 1 to 22 with no repeats (two were "12." and
    two "20."), the contents list matches them, and links into the guide from the
    audit, fix, template, convert, export and guidelines pages and from the FAQ,
    which pointed at anchors that did not exist, now land on the right section.
    scripts/build-doc-pages.py gains a render() function and a drop_title
    option, set for the guide, so the served page has one <h1>; the other five
    pages build exactly as before. New web/tests/test_user_guide_page.py checks
    one edition, one <h1>, section order, every link, and that the committed
    page matches its Markdown.
  • Documentation reads better with assistive technology. 38 code blocks in
    nine files now name their language; shell comments in web/README.md that
    rendered as eight top-level headings are now a real "OIDC and Keycloak
    integration" section; the deployment lifecycle and WSL staging diagrams have a
    description in words; the directory tree in CONTRIBUTING.md no longer uses
    box-drawing characters; and the user guide's second title, where an earlier
    edition follows the current one, is a level-two heading ("Earlier edition of
    this guide") until the two are merged (#147).

  • Contributor links. CONTRIBUTING.md and CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md no longer
    send people to GitHub Discussions, which are not enabled for this repository;
    they point to issues and the project contact address. CONTRIBUTING.md links
    the feedback form at letitglow.app.

  • Default web Fix runs no longer show a custom-settings warning for balanced
    heading detection. Disabling detection or changing its accuracy is still
    reported as a customization, with regression tests for both form inputs and
    normalized options.

  • Document browser regressions use a tracked sample on every platform, exercise
    the current conversion download links, and run without a separate job worker.
    The AHG browser checker records download connection failures without skipping
    the remaining reflow and accessibility checks.

  • Site Audit's deep scanner never ran in production, and said so unreadably.
    Every scanned page carried an AXE-UNAVAILABLE finding containing a raw npm
    permission trace, which the site owner could neither understand nor act on --
    and which was not a defect in their page at all. Three stacked causes: HOME
    is /app but only /app/instance and /app/.gunicorn were chowned, so npm
    could not create its cache at /app/.npm; @axe-core/cli was never installed
    in the image, so npx axe tried to download it at scan time, which is exactly
    what needed that cache; and the image had no browser for axe to drive. Every
    audit had therefore been running heuristics only. The cache directory is now
    created and owned by the runtime user, the axe CLI and Chromium are installed
    at build time, and axe runs with the flags a container needs. A scanner outage
    is no longer reported as a finding against the audited site: it is one
    run-level notice, in plain language, saying what could not run and what that
    means for the results, with the raw error tucked into a collapsed "technical
    details" section for whoever maintains the server.
    (Dockerfile,
    site_audit.py)

  • The audio transcription queue is shared across workers. Three defects came
    out of reviewing what had been dismissed as a per-worker design detail. Jobs
    could be stranded: _dispatch_queued_jobs() only drained the calling worker's
    local queue, so once the concurrency gate became global (above), a slot
    released on one worker never woke a job waiting on the other -- it could sit
    at "Queued..." while capacity was idle. The depth cap was per-worker, so the
    real queue was the configured depth times the worker count. And the queue
    position shown to a waiting user was the local index, so someone told they
    were second in line could actually be fifth -- a misleading wait for anyone,
    and a genuine accessibility problem for a screen reader user sitting on a long
    transcription. The queue is now one shared FIFO (Redis ZSET scored by enqueue
    time): an atomic enqueue makes the depth cap exact, ZRANK gives the true
    global position, and an atomic claim plus a per-worker sweeper lets any worker
    start any waiting job the moment capacity frees anywhere -- possible because
    job state and the audio file already live on shared storage. Without Redis it
    falls back to the original local queue.
    (routes/whisperer.py)
  • Site Audit submissions are bounded. The anonymous submit endpoint had no
    rate limit and spawned an unbounded thread per submission, each making up to
    max_pages outbound fetches -- one HTTP request became a crawler, and a burst
    became many. Submissions are now rate limited (6/min), and the number of scans
    running at once is capped (GLOW_MAX_CONCURRENT_SITE_AUDITS, default 4); a
    submission past the cap waits briefly for a slot and then reports a retryable
    "capacity is busy" state instead of parking a thread indefinitely.
    (routes/site_audit.py)
  • SSRF DNS-rebinding closed. The Site Audit and PageFlow fetch paths
    validated the target host name before fetching, but DNS could rebind to an
    internal address between that check and the socket connect. Both now fetch
    through a guarded session whose connections validate the actual peer IP inside
    connect() -- TOCTOU-free -- refusing loopback/private/link-local/reserved
    addresses at connect time without changing TLS/SNI/certificate behavior.
    (site_audit.py,
    listen_later.py)
  • AI concurrency gates count across workers. The chat/audio/vision gates
    limited simultaneous OpenRouter calls with in-process semaphores, so under two
    gunicorn workers the real cap was double the configured GLOW_MAX_*_SESSIONS
    and /health under-reported it. The gates now use a Redis-backed distributed
    semaphore (per-gate ZSET, atomic Lua acquire, TTL reclamation of slots leaked
    by crashed workers), resolved from the same Redis as the rate limiter, and
    degrade to the in-process semaphore when Redis is absent.
    (gating.py)
  • Background job pages work across gunicorn workers. Site Audit and
    Whisperer kept job state in a per-process in-memory dict, so under the
    production 2-worker deployment a follow-up request (status poll, cancel,
    retry, download, or an emailed Whisperer retrieval link opened later) that
    landed on the other worker 404'd about half the time. Both now persist each
    job to a per-job status.json on the shared instance volume (atomic write,
    strict UUID path-traversal guard, token hashes only -- never plaintext tokens
    or passwords), so any worker can serve status/cancel/retry/download/retrieve.
    (routes/site_audit.py,
    routes/whisperer.py)
  • Office add-in: 0 npm vulnerabilities and the build is fixed. Resolved the
    nanoid and browserslist Dependabot alerts (plus the rest of the
    dev-toolchain advisories) via overrides and a semver-safe npm audit fix,
    without a breaking downgrade of the sideload tooling. Fixed the pre-existing
    npm run build failure: src/version.ts read the filesystem at runtime
    (fs/path/__dirname), which cannot work in a browser task-pane bundle --
    the version is now injected at build time by webpack's DefinePlugin from the
    repo-root VERSION file. (office-addin/)
  • Codebase-wide bug-hunt second pass. A read-only audit surfaced ~40 further
    defects across seven subsystems; all were fixed with regression tests (full
    web suite green, 916 passing). Highlights: the chat "Compliance Agent" read a
    nonexistent Finding.description and compared severities in the wrong case,
    so it silently returned a regex heuristic instead of a real audit for every
    document (chat_handler.py); feature flags reset to their compiled defaults
    on every restart under the sqlite backend, silently re-enabling disabled
    features (app.py, feature_flags.py); the Whisperer worker's narrow
    except could freeze a job as "running" forever and stall the whole queue
    (routes/whisperer.py); the Playground streaming endpoint dropped every
    turn's history because it wrote to the session cookie from inside the response
    generator (routes/playground.py); PDF export handed back a 0-byte file with
    HTTP 200 on failure (chat_handler.py); a pronunciation-dictionary entry
    containing a backslash 500'd the request, and an extensionless upload could be
    deleted during text comparison (magic_features.py); uploaded zip/XML
    documents had no decompression-bomb caps (visual_items.py); the PageFlow
    reader was a second SSRF vector (routes/page_flow.py, listen_later.py);
    and a batch of front-end fixes -- a rules-reference null deref that could
    overwrite a saved rule set, a global tab handler that wiped unsaved admin-flag
    toggles and re-injected un-nonced script, an ai-meter that re-announced itself
    to screen readers once per second site-wide, and a job-progress stream with no
    error fallback. Session cookies now set HttpOnly/SameSite/Secure, admin logins
    regenerate the session, and request logs redact secret query parameters. See
    fixes.md for the full itemized list.
  • Whisperer could deadlock its whole worker when the audio queue filled. The
    "queue full" branch called a lock-taking helper while already holding the same
    non-reentrant lock, so the ninth concurrent submission would block forever
    holding it and wedge every route that touches the lock.
    (web/src/acb_large_print_web/routes/whisperer.py)
  • Site Audit crawler no longer follows mailto:/tel:/javascript: links or
    re-scans URL fragments.     _normalize_url prefixed any non-web string with
    https://, turning mailto:info@x into a bogus same-site "page"; and /page
    versus /page#section were treated as two pages, so in-page anchors burned
    the crawl budget. Non-web schemes are now rejected and fragments stripped.
    HTML error pages (status >= 400) are recorded as errors instead of counted as
    scanned pages, and the parser now flushes a missing or chunk-split </title>
    so compliant pages are not falsely reported as title-less.
    (web/src/acb_large_print_web/site_audit.py)
  • Quick Wins undercounted auto-fixable findings. Four entries in
    FIXABLE_RULE_IDS named rules that do not exist (ACB-BOLD-BODY,
    ACB-ALL-CAPS, ACB-HYPHENATION, ACB-DOC-LANG), so those findings were
    never shown as auto-fixable and the "Show Quick Wins Only" filter understated
    what GLOW Fix can do. Corrected to the real IDs and added a guard test.
    (web/src/acb_large_print_web/routes/audit.py)
  • The Site Audit live status page is now accessible. It had no live region,
    no real progress bar, disabled the focused Cancel button on completion, and
    its poller retried a dead job forever with no response.ok check. It now
    announces every state/progress/error change into a polite live region, drives
    a <progress> element, surfaces the error inline, stops after repeated
    failures, and moves focus to the results link instead of dropping it. The
    "Private Access" card no longer claims protection on unprotected runs.
    (web/src/acb_large_print_web/templates/site_audit_job.html)
  • The deploy post-check no longer fails a healthy deploy on a probe race.
    The external URL and CSP-header checks ran moments after Caddy restarts and a
    single early request could catch it mid-reload; both now retry with backoff.
    (scripts/post-deploy-check.sh)
  • Every ordinary Site Audit submission failed with "Working outside of
    application context."     The audit form's "run in background" box is checked by
    default, and the background path ran the scan on a bare threading.Thread
    whose worker called _runs_root() -- which reads current_app.instance_path
    -- after the request context that spawned it was gone. Flask raised
    RuntimeError, the worker caught it, and the job page reported the raw
    message as "Scan failed", which is what a user auditing a single page saw from
    two different machines. The thread body now runs inside app.app_context(),
    with the app object captured while the request is still live -- the same idiom
    the workshop pulse route already used. The background-job test previously
    stubbed the scanner and only checked the status endpoint's shape, so the
    swallowed error never failed it; it now waits for the job to finish and
    asserts a complete, error-free run, which fails against the old code.
    (web/src/acb_large_print_web/routes/site_audit.py,
    web/tests/test_site_audit.py)
  • The weekly strict accessibility audit has failed every scheduled run since
    2026-06-29 and nobody saw it,     because the strict step only runs on a
    schedule and every push-triggered run skipped it. Three pages failed -- user
    guide, workshop launchpad, workshop champion skill -- all reporting
    0 blocking axe violation(s). The gate was red on axe incomplete results,
    not measured failures; the real ratios were 17.4:1, 17.4:1 and 14.19:1. Two
    were an axe limitation with a legitimate cause: pre carried a 1px border and
    no padding, and axe bounds a scroll container at
    getBoundingClientRect().left + scrollWidth, counting neither the border nor
    the fraction scrollWidth truncates, so wrapped text landed 1-20px outside
    the box axe computed and it could not resolve the background. pre now has
    padding, which also stops text touching its own border. The audit passes
    locally under the exact CI environment: 43 tests, 38 pages, 0 violations.
  • Workshop launchpad showed readers raw <a href="..."> markup instead of
    links.     escape() returns Markup, and Markup.replace() escapes its
    replacement, so the anchors built in _render_tokenized_workflow_text were
    turned back into &lt;a href=...&gt; and rendered as visible text. The
    un-breakable URL inside then pushed the card past the right edge of the
    viewport -- a WCAG 1.4.10 Reflow failure at 1280px, worse at 320px -- which
    was the third strict-audit failure. Escaping now happens on a plain str and
    the trusted anchors are spliced in before re-wrapping, so untrusted text stays
    escaped; both behaviours have regression tests. .workshop-panel > dl > dd
    also gets overflow-wrap: anywhere, since the launchpad renders a bare <dl>
    that never picked up .workshop-field-list.
    (web/src/acb_large_print_web/routes/workshop.py)

  • Four dark-mode contrast failures, none of which CI could see. The
    accessibility gate audits the light theme only; dark mode is checked on the
    home page alone and only for violations, never incomplete. Found and fixed:
    the workflow tip (.workflow-banner, on audit, fix, convert, export and
    template) kept its light #f0f5ff background while text inherited #e0e0e0
    -- 1.21:1, with its link at 1.98:1; .flash-info/.flash-message had the
    same fault at 1.97:1 on the link; /changelog/ h3 headings computed
    #1a1a1a on #121212 across 94 nodes -- 1.07:1, effectively invisible;
    and pre/kbd/table kept background-color: #ffffff from the light rule
    with no dark counterpart, so a link crossing into a table sat at 2.16:1.
    All now 6.29:1 or better, most above 11:1. Callout borders moved from
    #1a4570 (1.90:1 against the page) to #4a90d9 (5.60:1), since the fill is
    only 1.07:1 and the border is the sole thing separating the callout from the
    page. Light mode is unchanged throughout.

  • Site Audit was unreachable from the home page, and unmentioned on the page
    that sends people looking for it.     Reported by a user who could not find
    where to submit a URL: the "Assess Accessibility" card promised "a document or
    website" but rendered its Site Audit link behind an {% elif %}, so the link
    only ever appeared when Document Audit was disabled -- which it never is.
    The same {% elif %} hid three further calls to action: Build a Template,
    Braille Studio, and the Whisperer. All four cards now render every enabled
    destination, wrapped in a .mission-card__links list so the targets stay
    visually and programmatically separable; without it two inline-block anchors
    sat about thirteen pixels apart with overlapping focus rings and a target
    height under the 24px of WCAG 2.5.8. Document Audit and Site Audit now also
    point at each other, so arriving at the wrong one costs a single click instead
    of a support email. Files:
    web/src/acb_large_print_web/templates/index.html,
    web/src/acb_large_print_web/templates/audit_form.html,
    web/src/acb_large_print_web/templates/site_audit_form.html,
    web/src/acb_large_print_web/static/forms.css.

  • Speech Studio Quick Start no longer loops back to "upload again" (issue
    #84).     When a document is prepared asynchronously, run_speech_prepare_job
    redirects the user back to /speech/?token=..., but the speech.speech_form
    GET handler did not restore the prepared state, so the page looked like a
    fresh, un-prepared upload and the Preview/Download actions stayed hidden — an
    apparent infinite upload loop. The handler now re-reads the persisted
    speech_prepare.json (validating the token match, required fields, and a
    non-empty extracted-text file) and passes it to the template, which emits a
    #speech-prepared-data JSON block that
    web/src/acb_large_print_web/static/speech.js
    reads on load to restore the estimate, prefill the preview text, and reveal
    the preview/download buttons. Also excluded internal pipeline files
    (speech_source.txt, speech_rendered.txt, speech_meta.json,
    speech_prepare.json) from the upload-session scan in speech_form and
    _resolve_document_source, so the original uploaded filename (not a generated
    speech_* file) is shown and re-prepared. Files:
    web/src/acb_large_print_web/routes/speech.py,
    web/src/acb_large_print_web/templates/speech.html,
    web/src/acb_large_print_web/static/speech.js.
    New regression tests in
    web/tests/test_speech_routes.py.
  • Live job progress now streams in real time through the reverse proxy.
    Added flush_interval -1 to the Caddy reverse_proxy for letitglow.app and
    narrowed encode gzip to a content-type allow-list so text/event-stream is
    never buffered or compressed. This affects every Server-Sent Events endpoint:
    job progress (convert, audit, fix, template, export, speech, page-flow), AI
    playground stream, speech stream, and the Ollama chat proxy. Previously the
    progress bar appeared frozen until the user manually refreshed.
    (web/Caddyfile)
  • SSE endpoints isolated from Caddy's encode handler. The compression
    middleware inspects response chunks before deciding to skip non-matching
    content types, and that inspection buffered small SSE writes (progress deltas,
    heartbeats) even though text/event-stream was already off the allow-list.
    Moved /job/*/status and /playground/stream into a dedicated @sse matcher
    that bypasses encode entirely. (web/Caddyfile)
  • Gunicorn switched from sync to gthread workers
    (--worker-class gthread --workers 2 --threads 16 --keep-alive 75). Sync
    workers serve one request per process, so each open SSE connection was holding
    one of four worker processes for up to the 30-minute stream timeout in
    web/src/acb_large_print_web/routes/jobs.py.
    Four concurrent progress viewers wedged the entire app. Threaded workers
    handle long-lived streams alongside normal page loads, raising effective
    concurrency from 4 to 32. (web/Dockerfile)
  • Job progress bar stuck at 20% in production because the page's
    progress-tracking JavaScript was an inline <script> block, which the site's
    Content-Security-Policy: script-src 'self' header silently blocks. The
    EventSource that drives the live progress UI was never created, so the bar
    never moved past the initial server-rendered value. Extracted the script to
    web/src/acb_large_print_web/static/job-progress.js
    and pass the SSE/poll URLs and initial state via data-* attributes on
    #job-progress-root in
    web/src/acb_large_print_web/templates/jobs/progress.html.
  • Maintenance mode toggle now reaches the web container. Added
    MAINTENANCE_MODE=${MAINTENANCE_MODE:-0} to the web service environment in
    web/docker-compose.prod.yml, so
    scripts/maintenance-mode.sh and scripts/deploy-app.sh can actually switch
    between the live site and the maintenance page. This fixes operator toggles
    that previously appeared to run but did not change app behavior.
  • Feature Flags CI import crash fixed for shared-core migration. Added a new
    compatibility bridge at
    web/src/acb_large_print_web/core_services.py
    that resolves audit_by_extension, fix_by_extension, and
    convert_to_markdown from quill_glow_core with per-symbol fallback to
    acb_large_print_core. Updated web routes/tasks (convert.py, speech.py,
    audit.py, fix.py, chat_handler.py, magic_features.py,
    tasks/convert_tasks.py) to import through the bridge so app startup and
    migrations no longer fail when quill_glow_core lacks convert_to_markdown.
  • Deploy workflow MCP test restored for markdown audits. Updated
    mcp_server/glow_mcp_utils.py to resolve core
    services from quill_glow_core with fallback to acb_large_print_core, so
    /audit markdown requests no longer fail with HTTP 400 when only the fallback
    core package is installed in CI.
  • About page now shows the shared core library version explicitly. The
    global template context now guarantees
    component_versions.shared_core_library (preferring quill-glow-core, then
    acb-large-print-core) and
    web/src/acb_large_print_web/templates/about.html
    displays that value for the "Shared service core package" field.
  • Production image builds now install shared core explicitly. Added a
    pip install of the quill-glow-core source archive in
    web/Dockerfile and
    mcp_server/Dockerfile before installing ./desktop,
    preventing deploy-time build failures when quill-glow-core is not resolvable
    from PyPI.
  • Queued uploads now persist across web and worker containers. Added
    GLOW_UPLOAD_TEMP_BASE=/app/instance/upload_temp for both web and worker
    in web/docker-compose.prod.yml, and made
    web/src/acb_large_print_web/upload.py
    honor that environment override. This keeps upload temp files in a shared
    writable volume and fixes queue jobs failing with
    Upload token ... not found or expired.

  • Audit queue handoff no longer deletes upload tokens before workers read
    them.     Updated
    web/src/acb_large_print_web/routes/audit.py
    so async audit submits preserve the upload token (skip request-finally
    cleanup) after enqueuing run_audit_job, preventing immediate
    Upload token ... not found or expired failures on /job/<id>/status.

  • Complete the AHG content consistency pass: seven-heading ready check, caption
    source text on both assistant paths, evidence limits, voluntary author credit,
    approved fallbacks and deferred sharing, a timed block-7 plan with partner
    review, and observable learning-outcome checks.

  • Celery worker tasks crashing with "Working outside of application
    context"    : The previous fix (celeryd_init signal calling create_app())
    was insufficient because the @celery_app.task decorators in
    convert_tasks.py execute at module-import time and bake in whatever
    celery_app.Task was at that moment (the default celery.Task). Reassigning
    celery_app.Task later did not retroactively rebind already-registered task
    classes. Rebuilt web/src/acb_large_print_web/tasks/__init__.py so
    ContextTask is a module-level class passed to
    Celery(..., task_cls=ContextTask) at app construction. Every
    @celery_app.task-decorated task (glow.convert, glow.pageflow_extract,
    glow.speech, glow.template, glow.export, glow.audit, glow.fix,
    glow.speech_prepare) now inherits the Flask-app-context wrapper regardless
    of import order. ContextTask also lazily bootstraps create_app() on first
    invocation as a safety net.

  • Complete the AHG content consistency pass: seven-heading ready check, caption
    source text on both assistant paths, evidence limits, voluntary author credit,
    approved fallbacks and deferred sharing, a timed block-7 plan with partner
    review, and observable learning-outcome checks.

  • Accessibility Regression Gate /guide/ contrast stability: strengthened
    code-block contrast for syntax-classed fenced code (pre > code.language-*)
    in web/src/acb_large_print_web/static/forms.css to prevent intermittent

  • Accessibility Regression SARIF workflow reliability: updated

Added

  • Add an AHG day-at-a-glance map in Markdown, HTML, Word and PowerPoint, with
    the seven stops, work locations, saved versions and approval-based sharing.

  • Add an optional, ten-minute ChatGPT Dots and Claude Duet closing demo with

    source attribution, 35 individual slide reviews, complete inline step-card

    slide-by-format evidence and scenario result tracking.

  • AHG 2026: a deck that meets people where they are. Block 1 grows from 20
    to 35 minutes (design is now 40, your agent at work 30) and seven slides: what
    you will be able to do, a ready check, a tour of the kit, a tour of the
    website, what makes up an agent, what automation can and cannot decide, where
    an agent plugs into work the office already does, and what you can use on
    Monday. 35 slides, none over 60 words on screen; the detail moved to the
    speaker notes. Every slide links to its step card, guide or page in the kit,
    in all four formats. The PowerPoint copy's smallest text is now 24 point, and
    nothing runs off a slide. In the HTML deck, "All slides" is a list of links
    instead of a dropdown that changed slide on every arrow press, each slide has
    its own address, and the arrow keys turn slides only in slide view. The byline
    is Jeff Bishop, University of Arizona, IT Accessibility Consultant, in
    collaboration with BITS and Techopolis, with thanks to Taylor Arndt. Every
    slide inside a block says where it is ("Block 4 of 7, slide 2 of 3"), and
    every hands-on slide says what to do if you are behind. A large print handout
    (slides-large-print-handout.docx, also a download on the deck page) carries
    the slides without notes and every link written out.

  • AHG 2026: agents in the work an office already does. The deck's "Plug it
    into the work you already do" slide, step card 7 and the tutorial's new
    "Putting it to work in your office" section ask the same four questions --
    what starts it, what it reads, where its draft goes, who signs off -- and
    /my-30-day-plan asks them too, with which assistant the campus approves and
    what information may go in.

  • AHG 2026: a check-in on the day, and the workshop in plain language.
    /ahg/check-in asks two questions and no name before lunch (how it is going,

    /ahg/check-in/results for the helpers, behind the survey's key.
    kit/session-in-plain-language.md says what the workshop is, who it is for
    and what you do in about 150 words, in four formats, linked from the AHG home
    page and the setup message. The run of show adds captions (CART, PowerPoint
    subtitles or Windows Live Captions) and both new pre-flight checks.

  • AHG 2026: the resource library, in every format.
    scripts/build_ahg_library.py builds one folder (S:\ahg by default) holding

    kit, the browser path texts, the sample course, the conference upload set, an

    Accessibility 1.1 metadata, checked with Ace by DAISY and EPUBCheck; DAISY
    comes from DAISY Pipeline 2, checked with its own validators.
    scripts/check_ahg_library.py checks the result, axe-core in Edge included.
    The Word copies now give each link its text as a ScreenTip, which the PDF
    carries as the link's description; the HTML copies wrap long paths at 320 px;
    GLOW's EPUB audit reads Ace 1.4's report and Pandoc's output on Windows

  • AHG 2026: every participant document in four formats, checked against
    primary sources, and a pre-workshop survey.     scripts/ahg_formats.py writes
    an HTML page, an ACB large print Word file and a reading deck beside each

    web/tests/test_workshop_ahg_formats.py check every copy, and
    docs/ahg-2026/formats.md is the inventory. Accessibility Agents is vendored
    at 2f4fe22 (113 skills). On 29 October 2026 every claim about tools and
    standards in the kit was checked against its primary source and the stale ones
    corrected: the Title II dates (26 April 2027 and 2028, from the Department of
    Justice interim final rule of 20 April 2026), where Claude Code finds skills,
    the chat.fontSize setting, the VS Code and Codex install lines, and the

    /ahg/survey/results with AHG_SURVEY_KEY, and are deleted by 31 January
    2027 (routes/ahg_survey.py, web/tests/test_ahg_survey.py).

  • Two enforced rules for accessibility reports and credits.
    .github/workflows/accessibility-reports.yml acknowledges each report,
    reminds the accessibility owner after 5 business days without a maintainer
    reply, reopens a report closed without an outcome, and invites the reporter to
    confirm a fix. .github/workflows/accessibility-credits.yml asks each outside
    contributor once how they want to be credited and records their answer;
    node .github/scripts/a11y-credits.mjs --since <tag> prints the release-notes
    block. The logic is .github/scripts/a11y-community.mjs, tested by
    .github/workflows/a11y-community-tests.yml. See "How we respond" in
    ACCESSIBILITY.md.

  • GLOW adopts the Open Source Accessibility Framework. All 24 of its actions
    are checked, which completes the checklist, not the work; the record, action
    by action, is in
    docs/accessibility-framework.md,
    and the first public progress update is
    docs/accessibility-progress.md.
    ACCESSIBILITY.md
    (formerly the crawl log accessibility.md) now states GLOW's priorities,
    contributor expectations, how to report a barrier, severity, how we respond,
    ownership, the dependencies that affect accessibility, supported environments
    and known limitations. The core web flows have a screen reader spot check
    (JAWS and NVDA, by the accessibility owner) and recorded manual checks. Open
    work: the desktop app and Word add-in (#146), checking tagged PDF output
    (#145), abbreviations on the core pages (#157) and a person's keyboard pass
    (#143). Thanks to @stickbear2015 and @brlgirl, whose reports fixed Speech
    Studio (#83, #84).
  • Accessibility issue form and pull request checklist.
    .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/accessibility.yml applies the accessibility label,
    asks four questions and never asks for disclosure; config.yml offers the
    feedback form and email instead. .github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md is new,
    with an accessibility checklist for content, interface, output documents and
    dependencies.
  • Keyboard-only smoke test and zoom and reflow check in CI.
    web/e2e/tests/keyboard.spec.mjs (npm run test:keyboard) walks each core
    page's tab sequence (every control reachable, a visible focus style, reading
    order, no trap) and completes audit, fix, convert and template with Tab, Enter
    and Space only. web/e2e/tests/reflow.spec.mjs (npm run test:reflow) checks
    six core pages at 640 and 320 CSS pixels (200 and 400 percent zoom). Both run
    in the Accessibility Regression Gate. What they check and what still needs a
    person is in
    docs/accessibility-testing.md.

  • Markdown accessibility lint. The Docs Quality workflow now runs
    markdownlint with the accessibility rules only (heading levels, one H1, alt
    text, link text, table shape, code block languages) on all documentation,
    configured in .github/a11y.markdownlint-cli2.jsonc.

  • Site Audit checks heading structure and page title quality. Two optional
    best-practice checks, on by default and switchable off, prompted by feedback
    from a screen reader user at the Carroll Center for the Blind: a page can pass
    every automated WCAG check and still be laborious to navigate. The heading
    check flags pages with no headings, a missing or repeated h1, skipped
    heading levels, headings that announce no text, pages whose content volume far
    outruns their heading count, and graphics apparently doing the visual job of
    section headings. The title check flags generic titles ("Home"), several pages
    in one run sharing a title, and titles that do not describe the page they
    belong to. These are reported and labelled as "Best practice", never as WCAG
    conformance failures, so a conformance report stays readable.
    (site_audit.py)

  • Every finding now carries plain-language guidance. Each result explains
    what to actually do about it, in the results table and in the CSV export,
    alongside a column saying whether it is a WCAG conformance failure or a best
    practice. A rule id and a WCAG number tell a specialist what happened; these
    tell everyone else.
    (site_audit.py)

  • The GLOW passport -- one optional identity for the whole product: settings
    that follow a person to another device via a single-use emailed link, with no
    password and no account. Preferences previously lived in one browser's local
    storage and evaporated on a phone or after a cookie clear, which fell hardest
    on the people who had most carefully tuned their type scale, contrast mode and
    cognitive profile. Optional at every point; GLOW is unchanged for anyone who
    never uses it. History is opt-in only, deleted when switched off; retention is
    90 days from last use; one control deletes everything and says what it
    deleted. See docs/PASSPORT.md.

  • Workshop Mode and the passport are one identity. Joining a workshop
    attaches the participant to the passport this browser carries, and the display
    name is remembered. Gallery anonymity is untouched.
  • Whisperer notification address is remembered when notifications are on,
    instead of being retyped for every job.

  • Email status and a test send on the admin queue page: what mail can do,
    which sender and stream, and one message that proves the path without waiting
    for a real event.

  • Celery worker liveness in /health and Docker healthcheck:
    web/src/acb_large_print_web/app.py now probes the Celery worker pool via
    celery_app.control.inspect().ping() and includes a new worker entry in
    both services and readiness. When CELERY_BROKER_URL is configured but no
    workers respond, /health flips to degraded, which causes
    scripts/deploy-app.sh and scripts/post-deploy-check.sh to fail fast
    instead of marking a deploy as complete while jobs silently stall in Queued
    state. Added a corresponding Docker healthcheck to the worker service in
    web/docker-compose.prod.yml (runs
    celery -A acb_large_print_web.tasks inspect ping) so Docker surfaces a
    wedged worker for the restart: unless-stopped policy. Eager-mode (no broker)
    deployments report not-configured and remain green.

  • Queue-first heavy workflow expansion across the web app: extended the
    shared /job/<id>/ progress model beyond Convert to include Export, Template
    generation, Speech document preparation, Speech document/typed downloads,
    PageFlow extraction, single-file Audit submit, and non-interactive Fix runs.
    Added new queued task handlers in
    web/src/acb_large_print_web/tasks/convert_tasks.py plus retry dispatch
    support for these operations.

  • PageFlow queued extraction handoff: added queued extraction operation
    support and a completion route (/page-flow/from-job/<job_id>) so users can
    resume in the editable PageFlow text screen after background extraction
    completes.
  • Job progress continue actions: added optional continue_url support in
    job status payloads and progress UI so queued preprocess workflows can guide
    users back to the correct next step.
  • Queue route regression coverage: added web/tests/test_queue_routes.py to
    validate queue path behavior for Template, Export, Speech Prepare, Audit, and
    Fix.

Security

  • Refresh the web accessibility tooling and its transitive dependencies,
    including a patched FTP parser used by the browser driver downloader.
  • Update the MCP server's multipart parser to 0.0.31 to address parsing
    denial-of-service and parameter-smuggling advisories.

  • Refresh Office add-in dependencies and development tools. Runtime dependencies
    audit clean; unpatched development-tool advisories remain tracked in
    issue 124.

  • Site Audit no longer fetches internal addresses (SSRF fix). The auditor
    fetched whatever URL an anonymous visitor submitted and packed the response
    body into the downloadable artifacts.zip, so a request for
    http://169.254.169.254/... or http://redis:6379/ would let the submitter
    read cloud-metadata credentials and internal services. Added an
    _is_public_url gate (rejects loopback, private, link-local, reserved,
    multicast addresses and non-web ports) and an _http_get wrapper that
    re-validates every redirect hop and caps the response body at 8 MB against
    decompression bombs. All three fetch sites (scan, crawl, sitemap) go through
    it, and the sitemap XML is now parsed with defusedxml.
    (web/src/acb_large_print_web/site_audit.py)

  • Rate-limit keys can no longer be rotated to bypass the brute-force caps.
    rate_limit_key keyed on the glow_workshop_participant cookie for every
    route, so an attacker sending a fresh random cookie per request got a new
    bucket each time -- defeating the admin-login 10/min cap and the upload caps.
    The cookie key is now scoped to workshop routes only; everywhere else keys on
    the remote address.
    (web/src/acb_large_print_web/app.py)

  • Closed an open redirect in the consent gate. The next guard was
    bypassable with HTTPS://evil.com (case) and /\evil.com (backslash).
    Replaced with a positive same-site test; the consent page is the first page a
    new visitor sees, so this was a strong phishing lure.
    (web/src/acb_large_print_web/routes/consent.py)

  • Per-request CSP nonces, site-wide. The production
    Content-Security-Policy was script-src 'self'; style-src 'self', which
    silently blocked every inline <script> and <style> block in the templates
    and every inline on*= event handler. Most pages had subtle JS-feature
    breakage (the same class of bug that froze the job progress bar at 20%). Moved
    CSP emission from web/Caddyfile into a Flask after_request
    hook in
    web/src/acb_large_print_web/app.py so
    each response gets a fresh secrets.token_urlsafe(16) nonce stashed on
    g.csp_nonce, exposed to Jinja as csp_nonce, and injected into script-src
    and style-src. Added nonce="{{ csp_nonce }}" to all 20 inline <script>
    blocks and 3 inline <style> blocks across the templates (base.html,
    audit_form.html, fix_form.html, settings.html, admin_*,
    chat_form.html, convert_form.html, rules_ref.html, maintenance.html,
    etc.). External scripts continue to match 'self' and need no nonce. Added
    script-src-attr 'none' as defense-in-depth against any future inline event
    handlers, and style-src-attr 'unsafe-inline' so style attributes
    (style="display:none") used throughout the markup keep working without a
    churn-heavy refactor.

  • Inline event handlers refactored to delegated listeners. All 15 remaining
    onclick/oninput attributes (return confirm(...), history.back(),
    glowToggleRuleGroup(this, ...), the chat character-count mirror) were
    replaced with data-confirm, data-action="history-back",
    data-toggle-rule-group="select|deselect", and
    data-char-count-target/data-char-count-max attributes. A new
    web/src/acb_large_print_web/static/inline-handlers.js,
    loaded from base.html, wires them up via delegated event listeners on
    document. Templates touched: admin_requests.html, admin_speech.html,
    admin_queue.html, admin_flags.html, audit_form.html, fix_form.html,
    chat_form.html, privacy.html, error.html, feedback_thanks.html. No
    'unsafe-inline' or 'unsafe-hashes' in script-src.
  • Deduplicated security headers between Caddy and Flask. Production
    responses were emitting X-Content-Type-Options, X-Frame-Options, and
    Referrer-Policy twice (once from Caddy, once from Flask), and the two
    X-Frame-Options values disagreed (DENY from Caddy versus SAMEORIGIN from
    Flask). Removed those three directives from the letitglow.app and @sse
    blocks in web/Caddyfile and let Flask's existing
    _add_security_headers after_request hook own them. Caddy continues to emit
    only the transport-level / policy headers it should own
    (Strict-Transport-Security, Permissions-Policy).

Changed

  • Clarify the AHG step cards, facilitator and helper guidance, kit welcome
    page and deck: use one browser conversation, review versions after blocks
    3 to 5, verify evidence, and check a draft 30-day plan before saving it.

  • Let browser-path participants save each agent version locally on
    /ahg/assistant, with review controls next to blocks 3 to 5, keyboard and
    clipboard fallbacks, and explicit instructions not to overwrite earlier
    downloads. The online and offline share pages warn that opening GitHub's
    form sends the agent text before submission.

  • Job progress page auto-advances on success. When a queued job completes
    and a continue_url is set (e.g., PageFlow handing off to the narration
    page), the universal progress screen now announces "Done. Continuing\u2026"
    and navigates to the next step after a short delay. Any click or keypress
    cancels the auto-advance so users who want the Download or Continue link still
    control the page.
    (web/src/acb_large_print_web/templates/jobs/progress.html)

  • Speech voice selection simplified: Speech Studio now uses one combined
    voice combo box across ready engines instead of grouped radio clusters, and
    corresponding client-side state handling now reads/writes a single selected
    value.

  • PageFlow voice selection simplified: PageFlow narration voice selection
    now uses one combined voice combo box and removed engine-filter UI/script
    complexity.
  • Speech prepare queue API response: queued Speech document preparation now
    returns JSON (202 with job_url) for fetch-based UI flows, while preserving
    synchronous fallback behavior when queueing is unavailable.
  • Canonical web domain defaults moved to letitglow.app across
    deployment/runtime config: updated production Caddy routing, deploy script
    defaults, post-deploy checks, Keycloak hostname default, and
    maintenance/status helper guidance to use letitglow.app as the primary host
    while preserving legacy host behavior.
  • Legacy host redirect policy finalized with GGG exception: legacy app hosts
    now redirect to canonical letitglow.app for normal routes, but continue to
    serve /ggg* directly so existing externally shared podcast/workshop
    distribution links keep working without redirect churn.
  • Community Access is now the default public branding profile: switched
    default GLOW_BRAND_PROFILE behavior from bits to communityaccess, added
    Community Access logo asset, updated footer/org copy, and adjusted
    public-facing consent/about/privacy/guidelines wording toward neutral
    attribution.
  • OpenRouter referer and email sender defaults aligned to migration plan:
    OpenRouter HTTP-Referer defaults now use https://letitglow.app, and
    Postmark default sender moved to no-reply@notify.letitglow.app.

  • AI Playground streaming responses (SSE) at /beta/chat/stream for
    token-by-token output rendering with automatic fallback to the legacy JSON
    endpoint when streaming is unavailable.
  • AI Playground quick controls: regenerate response, stop generation,
    in-page model switcher, prompt templates, session quota banner, and
    conversation export as Markdown.
  • MarkItDown audio conversion choice for short MP3/WAV uploads in the web
    Convert and Quick Start flows, so users can pick direct Markdown extraction
    for short clips while still using BITS Whisperer for larger recordings and
    broader audio format support.
  • Alt-Text Helper at /alt-text/ for AI-assisted alternative text drafting
    across standalone image files, Word, PowerPoint, Excel, PDF, and EPUB uploads.
    Quick Start and audit results can now hand visual-rich files directly into
    this workflow.
  • Alt-Text Helper variant generation: /alt-text/ now supports style
    selection (balanced, concise, detailed, instructional, narrative),
    multi-option suggestion generation (1/3/5), and optional per-page
    system-prompt add-ons for more diverse, controllable alt-text drafting.
  • AI request cost preview endpoint at /ai/usage/estimate so Document Chat
    and AI Playground can show rough token and price estimates before sending.
  • Async conversion queue for web Convert with Celery tasks, Redis-backed
    broker support, and a new /job route family for progress pages, SSE status
    streams, JSON polling, and secure result downloads.
  • Job progress accessibility regression tests in
    web/tests/test_jobs_accessibility.py covering core semantics, missing-job
    404 handling, poll responses, and result download behavior.
  • Workshop facilitator dashboard and delivery surfaces: added
    /workshop/session/<code>/facilitator with live participation metrics and
    activity snapshots, plus explicit /coach, /review, and /share surfaces
    for workshop workflow handoffs.
  • Workshop multi-format artifact exports: added JSON (/export/json), HTML
    (/export/html), and DOCX (/export/docx) exports in addition to existing
    markdown exports, and wired these into gallery/share/facilitator navigation.
  • Workshop route coverage tests in web/tests/test_workshop_routes.py
    validating facilitator/coach/review/share routes and export endpoints.
  • Workshop follow-through persistence: added
    /workshop/session/<code>/follow-through plus follow-through markdown export
    so users can save coaching templates, checklists, and 30-day commitments from
    workshop outputs.
  • Workshop follow-through discovery: surfaced Workshop Follow-Through links
    in the main sidebar and homepage mission grid so users can continue after the
    workshop without hunting for the entry point.
  • Workshop sidebar placement refined: moved the Workshop Follow-Through
    sidebar entry from the Experimental group into Explore and Learn so
    navigation aligns with workshop learning workflows.
  • Workshop follow-through tests in web/tests/test_workshop_routes.py
    validating saved commitments and exported follow-through markdown.
  • Workshop interactive activity passport and structured forms: upgraded
    /workshop/session/<code>/activity/<activity_key> with guided per-activity
    prompts, progress passport tracking, badge-style completion cues, and "save
    and continue" flow so workshop delivery feels more magical and hands-on while
    preserving export/follow-through compatibility.
  • Workshop conference-code and identity flow: updated /workshop/ to a
    two-step join journey (code lookup first, participant name second), added
    conference-code mappings via instance/workshop_conference_codes.json and
    WORKSHOP_CONFERENCE_CODES_JSON, and issued persistent guest participant
    tokens so people can return to their personal workshop content without login.
  • Workshop personal content surface: added /workshop/session/<code>/me to
    show participant-specific submissions resolved from the guest token, with
    optional OIDC email binding when user login is available.
  • Workshop magical launchpad with tokenized workflows: added
    /workshop/session/<code>/launchpad with scenario cards, downloadable sample
    documents from samples/, tokenized [[GLOW:...]] workflow steps, and deep
    links into Audit/Fix/Convert/Template/Chat/Alt-Text/Magic tools.
  • Cross-GLOW workshop return links: added global workshop_return /
    workshop_label query handling in base.html for linked tool pages, now
    gated to active workshop participants so non-workshop users do not see
    workshop-return UI.
  • WCAG language processing for Convert uploads: added deterministic language
    checks for uploaded/converted content (WCAG 3.1.1, 2.4.4, 3.3.2 plus
    plain-language long-sentence heuristics), configurable timing (off, input,
    output, both) and enforcement (advisory, strict) in
    web/src/acb_large_print_web/templates/convert_form.html, result reporting in
    web/src/acb_large_print_web/templates/convert_result.html, and
    default-enabled feature flags GLOW_ENABLE_WCAG_LANGUAGE_PROCESSING /
    GLOW_ENABLE_WCAG_LANGUAGE_STRICT_MODE.
  • Convert format coverage expanded: added legacy Office binary support for
    .doc and .ppt plus plain-text .txt across the Convert stack by extending
    MarkItDown convertible inputs (desktop/src/acb_large_print/converter.py),
    adding LibreOffice pre-conversion mappings for legacy binaries
    (desktop/src/acb_large_print/pandoc_converter.py), and enabling chained
    Pandoc output routes from those formats
    (web/src/acb_large_print_web/routes/convert.py and
    web/src/acb_large_print_web/upload.py).
  • Presidio PII guardrails for AI routes: added server-side PII sanitization
    for AI-bound text in Document Chat and alt-text suggestion routes (/chat/,
    /alt-text/suggest, and /audit/suggest-alt-text) via
    web/src/acb_large_print_web/pii_guardrails.py, added default-on feature
    flags GLOW_ENABLE_PII_GUARDRAILS / GLOW_ENABLE_PII_GUARDRAILS_STRICT_MODE,
    wired the new flags into the admin feature-flags UI, and added Presidio
    dependencies in web/requirements.txt and web/pyproject.toml.
  • Unified async orchestration controls for long-running jobs: added
    retry/deadline/cancel semantics for Convert and Site Audit background jobs,
    including convert job metadata and retry dispatch support
    (web/src/acb_large_print_web/tasks/convert_tasks.py), shared async policy
    loading (web/src/acb_large_print_web/async_orchestration.py), new
    cancel/retry job routes (web/src/acb_large_print_web/routes/jobs.py and
    web/src/acb_large_print_web/routes/site_audit.py), and progress-page
    controls in web/src/acb_large_print_web/templates/jobs/progress.html and
    web/src/acb_large_print_web/templates/site_audit_job.html.
  • GGG podcast static-site deployment integration: added a new ggg static
    service in web/docker-compose.prod.yml, routed lp.csedesigns.com/ggg*
    traffic to that service in web/Caddyfile, and added
    scripts/deploy-ggg-content.sh for targeted content sync. Standard production
    deploys now also run an optional server-local GGG sync inside
    scripts/deploy-app.sh (source ~/ggg to destination ~/app/ggg by
    default), regenerate/validate the feed when Node.js is available, and keep MP3
    media out of GitHub.

Changed

  • Admin auth gate test-mode compatibility: Updated

  • Homepage 7.2.0 "What's New" now includes MCP docs link: Updated

  • Office Add-in dependency security remediation: Updated

  • WCAG gate status wiring in deploy pipeline: Updated
    .github/workflows/deploy.yml to resolve the Accessibility Regression Gate

    points.

    token/cost preview text before request submission when model pricing is
    available.
  • Admin AI settings now support a rolling per-session AI request cap and
    reset window in addition to the existing monthly budget and workload-specific
    limits.
  • MarkItDown capability coverage now includes packaged support for all
    upstream extras in both the desktop and web Python package metadata, aligning
    installed behavior with the broader conversion formats already documented by
    MarkItDown upstream.
  • Quick Start audio routing now offers both Convert and BITS Whisperer for
    .mp3 and .wav files, while keeping longer or broader audio workflows on
    Whisperer.

Fixed

  • Complete the AHG content consistency pass: seven-heading ready check, caption
    source text on both assistant paths, evidence limits, voluntary author credit,
    approved fallbacks and deferred sharing, a timed block-7 plan with partner
    review, and observable learning-outcome checks.

  • Convert pipeline false-negative failure in CI: Updated
    web/src/acb_large_print_web/routes/convert.py so WCAG language text
    extraction fails open when MarkItDown cannot parse a generated output artifact
    (for example, mocked or malformed EPUB bytes), preventing successful
    conversions from returning HTTP 500.

  • Rules Reference accessibility filters: Removed a stale duplicate Type
    filter on /rules/ that reused id="filter-type", resolving axe
    duplicate-id-aria and form-field-multiple-labels findings.
  • Quick Start contrast review noise: Replaced gradient upload-hero
    backgrounds with solid high-contrast surfaces and added explicit foreground
    colors to file/text inputs and textareas so axe can calculate contrast
    reliably.
  • Crawl accessibility cleanup: Removed the remaining public raw Markdown
    deployment link, replaced decorative workflow banner glyphs, converted
    symbolic keyboard labels to text, and normalized code/table/textarea surfaces
    so automated contrast tools can compute foreground/background colors more
    reliably.
  • Documentation contrast review noise: Hardened documentation table and
    code-block layout so long content wraps inside its own painted box instead of
    visually overlapping adjacent cells or partially obscuring code text during
    axe color-contrast analysis.
  • Deployment guide code blocks: Kept generated <pre><code> snippets from
    exposing the inner code element as a block-level box, clearing axe
    color-contrast incomplete checks caused by the scroll container partially
    covering bash examples.
  • Public documentation links: Replaced raw .md documentation links in
    web-facing guide, FAQ, and PRD pages with HTML routes, and added
    /deployment/ as the public deployment guide page.
  • Audit and Template heading order: Promoted top-level in-content headings
    on /audit/ and /template/ to h2, resolving axe heading-order findings
    from same-origin urlCheck crawls.
  • AI usage meter landmark: The inactive AI meter now exposes the same
    complementary landmark semantics as active meter states, resolving axe
    region findings on the consent page.
  • Web App Color Contrast: Darkened low-contrast sidebar, breadcrumb, grade,
    copied-button, and disabled-button colors in
    web/src/acb_large_print_web/static/forms.css; added missing dark-mode
    overrides for file inputs, upload drop zones, AI panels, action cards, chat
    turns, and progress panels so core GLOW pages remain readable in dark theme.
  • Feature Flags CI failures now pass the web landmark guardrail again after
    removing redundant section[aria-labelledby] markup from the Alt-Text Helper
    and audit report templates, and the workflow now also triggers when its
    desktop or config-check dependencies change.
  • AI Playground character counter no longer announces every keystroke to
    screen readers while typing. The counter still updates visually and remains
    available through the textarea description without repeated live-region
    interruptions.
  • AI Playground response cards now keep model/copy controls after the
    response text instead of embedding them in the response heading, and assistant
    message wrappers no longer add extra spoken labels beyond the heading
    structure.
  • AI usage meter now increments correctly for Ollama-backed chat turns by
    reading the current quota field returned by the server.
  • AI Playground long-running responses now announce progress to screen
    reader users after a delay and announce completion when a delayed response
    arrives, instead of relying only on the visible thinking indicator.
  • Server-side AI feature gates now recognize built-in server-provider paths
    for alt-text and Whisperer instead of requiring a personal provider session
    before those features can appear.
  • Legacy alt-text suggestion endpoint no longer stops at DOCX media only. It
    now uses the shared visual extractor so PowerPoint, Excel, PDF, EPUB, and
    standalone image workflows stay aligned.
  • Quick Start and Speech Studio routing no longer advertise document-chat or
    speech actions for uploaded audio files that are outside those workflows.
  • Job progress page semantics now provide clearer live-region and progress
    labeling (aria-labelledby, aria-describedby, assertive error alerts, and
    hidden-state download toggling) to improve screen reader behavior during queue
    updates.

Security

Fixed

  • Complete the AHG content consistency pass: seven-heading ready check, caption
    source text on both assistant paths, evidence limits, voluntary author credit,
    approved fallbacks and deferred sharing, a timed block-7 plan with partner
    review, and observable learning-outcome checks.

  • Markdown to PDF styling cascade now preserves ACB formatting.
    desktop/src/acb_large_print/pandoc_converter.py now embeds PDF CSS using
    Pandoc --include-in-header in the intermediate HTML, then renders that HTML
    directly with WeasyPrint. This prevents Pandoc default styling from overriding
    ACB heading/list/link styles in PDF output.

  • DOCX conversion line wrapping and LibreOffice input support improved.
    Added --wrap=none for Pandoc DOCX generation to avoid soft-wrap line breaks
    in generated XML. Added .fodt as a native Pandoc input and added
    .ods/.fods/.odp/.fodp upload support with optional LibreOffice
    pre-conversion (soffice) into .xlsx/.pptx before the existing
    MarkItDown-to-Pandoc chain.

  • PDF tables now preserved in Word / HTML / EPUB exports. When a PDF
    containing embedded tables is uploaded and converted to Word (.docx), HTML,
    EPUB, or any other Pandoc-backed output format, the tables are now extracted
    as Markdown pipe tables and included in the output document. Previously,
    MarkItDown's pdfminer.six text extraction silently dropped all table
    structure, producing flat text. The fix adds _pdf_to_markdown_with_tables()
    to desktop/src/acb_large_print/converter.py, which uses PyMuPDF's
    find_tables() API (already a project dependency) to detect and format table
    cells, interleave them with surrounding text in reading order, and skip
    duplicate raw text blocks that fall inside table bounding boxes. Falls back
    transparently to MarkItDown if PyMuPDF is unavailable. 18 new unit tests added
    in desktop/tests/test_pdf_table_extraction.py.

  • Compare endpoint extension mismatch. POST /magic/compare now uses an
    explicit allow-list aligned with its UI and parser support (.txt, .csv,
    .json, .xml, .html, .rst, .odt, .rtf, plus existing types) instead
    of defaulting to the narrower upload allow-list.

  • PyMuPDF lifecycle robustness. magic_features.detect_reading_order_pdf()
    and magic_features.ocr_pdf() now compute pages_scanned before closing the
    document handle, avoiding access to len(doc) after doc.close().

  • Fix result re-audit flow hardening.
    web/src/acb_large_print_web/templates/fix_result.html now submits the
    re-audit action through a CSRF-protected POST form to /audit/from-fix,
    including token, filename, standards profile, and prior finding context. Added
    regression coverage in web/tests/test_fix_routes.py.

  • Public release documentation sync for v4.0.0. Updated canonical release
    and public-facing docs to align version messaging across changelog,
    announcements, combined announcement artifacts, PRD status, roadmap header,
    and user guide release framing.

  • Comprehensive axe-core WCAG 2.2 AA audit of GLOW itself. Added

    @axe-core/playwright test suite that audits all 17 public routes at WCAG 2.2
    AA level on every CI run. Pages audited include the 5 previously covered
    (home, audit, fix, convert, template) plus 12 new routes: Speech Studio,
    Braille Studio, Settings, Guidelines, User Guide, About, Changelog, FAQ, Rules
    Reference, Feedback, Privacy Policy, and Status. Additionally audits four
    interactive states: help accordions open, speech/braille unavailable banners,
    dark mode (prefers-color-scheme: dark), and mobile viewport (375 × 812 px).
    Critical and serious violations fail the CI build immediately with
    selector-level diagnostic output. Moderate and minor violations are surfaced
    as advisory warnings without blocking the build. Added
    @axe-core/playwright ^4.11.2 to web/package.json. Added test:axe npm
    script that runs only the axe spec (separate from the functional regression

    match all 17 routes for the SARIF secondary scan. Axe results are written to
